newsitem.title: USA: For movie on himself, Clinton would cast Tom Hanks.
newsitem.headline: For movie on himself, Clinton would cast Tom Hanks.

text.p: President Bill Clinton says he would cast contemporary superstar Tom Hanks to portray him if a movie were being made about his life.

"I mean, we don't look alike, and we're not the same size and shape or anything, but I know him and I respect him as a person and as an actor," Clinton said. "I would want somebody with a lot of range and a lot of human feeling."
He made the comments in an interview by Gene Siskel, film critic for the CBS News programme "This Morning," to be broadcast on Tuesday.

Clinton said he would choose another award-winning performer, Meryl Streep, to portray his wife, Hillary Rodham Clinton. Of Streep, he said: "She's a phenomenally gifted actress. ... She is extraordinary."
The president estimated he had seen the movie "High Noon," starring Gary Cooper, more than 20 times.
He admitted: "I probably go to too many movies. But you know, the great perk of the White House is the movie theatre."
"I loved Gary Cooper as a small boy ... 'High Noon.' I've seen it probably more than 20 times since 1951 or '52 when it came out," Clinton said.

"I loved it. ... He was the most realistic of all heroes. ... He doesn't have to say a word. You can look in his eyes and know that he thinks the chances are overwhelming that he's going to be killed, and he hates it. He wants to run off with Grace Kelly and have his life, but he does it anyway."
Cooper was a long-lasting Hollywood star who projected honest determination. He won a special Academy Award in 1960 for his performances and contribution to the film industry.
